translationRepairs: Sima Xiuzhi, whose courtesy name was Jiyu, was a native of Wen in Henan Commandery and a descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Yi, the younger brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan.
Sima Xiuzhi, whose courtesy name was Jiyu, was a native of Wen in Henei Commandery and a descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Xun, the younger brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan.
河內 is Henei, not Henan; 遜 is Xun, not Yi (懿). The English wrongly identifies the Prince of Qiao as Sima Yi.
Sima Xiuzhi, styled Jiyu, was originally a man of Wen in Henan, a descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Yi, the younger brother of the fourth rank of Jin's Emperor Xuan.
Sima Xiuzhi, styled Jiyu, was originally a man of Wen in Henei, a descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Xun, the younger brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan.
Same errors: 河內→Henei, 遜→Xun; 'fourth rank' garbles 季弟 (younger brother).

After Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Xiuzhi and Wensi, together with Prince Daoci of Hejian, Aid-the-State General Wen Kai, Jingling Interior Secretary Lu Gui, Jing provincial aides Han Yanzhi and Yin Yue, Pacify-the-West staff officers Huan Mi and Huan Lin, Huan Wen's grandsons Daodu and Daozi, Diao Yong of Bohai, Yuan Shi of Chen commandery, and several hundred others, all came with their families to surrender to Changsun Song.

After Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Xiuzhi and Wensi, together with Prince Daoci of Hejian, Aid-the-State General Wen Kai, Jingling Interior Secretary Lu Gui, Jing provincial aides Han Yanzhi and Yin Yue, Pacify-the-West staff officers Huan Mi and Huan Sui, Huan Wen's grandsons Daodu and Daozi, Diao Yong of Bohai, Yuan Shi of Chen commandery, and several hundred others, all came with their families to surrender to Changsun Song.
璲 is Sui (Suì), not Lin; English wrongly renders 桓璲 as Huan Lin.
He was posthumously made General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right, with the posthumous title Duke of Shisheng of Shiping."
He was posthumously made General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right, with the posthumous title Duke Sheng of Shiping."
始平聲公 is Duke Sheng of Shiping (posthumous name 聲), not "Duke of Shisheng of Shiping".
Under Emperor Xiaowen, Yue and others upheld Yi's claim as legitimate heir, and he recovered the ancestral title.
Under Emperor Xuanwu (Shizong), Yue and others upheld Yi's claim as legitimate heir, and he recovered the ancestral title.
世宗 is Emperor Xuanwu, not Xiaowen (高祖/孝文帝). English mistranslates the temple name.
Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Yu.
Early in Emperor Xuanwu's (Shizong) reign he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Yu.
世宗 is Xuanwu, not Xiaowen.
